newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up on Eurobond, London Club news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up on Eurobond, London Club news.

text.p: Western investors bought Russian shares on Friday after Moscow announced details for its Eurobond issue and debt rescheduling, lifting the market out of its recent doldrums, traders said.

LUKoil bounced to $9.45 from $8.97 at Thursday's close on the Russian Trading System (RTS). Mosenergo rose to $0.957 from $0.930. Rostelekom firmed to $2.51 from $2.42, and UES rose to $0.0797 from $0.0753.
The RTS index of 21 shares rose 3.41 percent to 171.72 on $18.2 million volume.
"The rise was due to the news of the Eurobond and the London Club," said Anton Kudryashov of Renaissance Capital.

Russia said it would issue a Eurobond in late October or early November and the Finance Ministry said it had reached a crucial agreement with Western creditor commercial banks, the London Club, on rescheduling $20 billion of debt, paving the way for a global agreement on its total $35 billion debt.
Traders said the stock market's rally would probably continue into next week but could falter.
Alexei Genkin of Alfa-Capital said investors jumped into the market to buy cheap shares while they could.
"Western investors had been waiting for the prices of leading shares to fall," he said.

Prices had fallen since President Boris Yeltsin announced last week he would have heart surgery at the end of the month. Western investors, who drive the market, held off on political uncertainty, traders said.
Some said that the week-long fall had been prolonged by investors who were eager to snap up cheap shares but were waiting for the lowest possible prices.
But traders said the market had not overcome its fears about Yeltsin's health.

"We are going to have some sort of rise before the operation but it is very possible... there will be sellers into the operation -- just in case. There are always people who want to hedge themselves," said Nick Mokhoff of Alliance-Menatep.
But he predicted the rally would continue into next week. "I would put money in the fact that Monday morning will see another rise," Mokhoff said.
